info.name: Healthcare Backend API
info.description:
Automated walk-through of the Healthcare Backend API (WhatBytes assignment).

Run every folder in order. Each run registers two new users (A and B) with unique emails, captures their JWTs and the ids it creates, checks status codes and response bodies, and finally deletes the patient, doctor and mapping it created. The two users stay, because the API has no endpoint for deleting users.

Run it with Newman (Node.js required). Either let npx download Newman:

    npx --yes newman@6.2.3 run postman/healthcare-backend.postman_collection.json --env-var "baseUrl=http://127.0.0.1:8000" --reporters cli --bail

or, if npx fails, install Newman into a temporary folder outside the project and run it from there:

    npm install --prefix <temporary folder> newman@6.2.3
    <temporary folder>/node_modules/.bin/newman run postman/healthcare-backend.postman_collection.json --env-var "baseUrl=http://127.0.0.1:8000" --reporters cli --bail

`baseUrl` defaults to http://127.0.0.1:8000; override it as above or in Postman. The password variable is a fake value used only for these test accounts. Token and id variables start empty and are filled during the run.

Note: in /api/mappings/<id>/ the number is a PATIENT id for GET and a MAPPING id for DELETE.
